finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the query parameter f is joined to /srv/files with filepath.Join, which cleans '..' segments but does not confine the result to root. An unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary files readable by the process.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'f' on GET /dl (files.go:12), attacker-controlled
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response body written at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl is registered to download with no authentication middleware
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, which escapes root
file contents returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check after Join, no filepath.Base, no rejection of '..' or absolute paths, no authentication, and no os.Root or fs.FS confinement. Join cleaning does not prevent escape. The error path only returns 404 and does not block the read. Repro: GET /dl?f=../../etc/passwd

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the raw query param f into filepath.Join("/srv/files", name) and os.ReadFile with no prefix check, Base, or auth (files.go:32 registers /dl bare), so ../../etc/passwd escapes root and files.go:18 returns the contents.
